scope: Full daily Power Stack research refresh across all tracked categories, existing ideas, US/Hong Kong-China/Malaysia and every canonical holding. Research/data only.
decision: One material holding change: IOIPG fundamental score 74 provisional to 78/B after FY26 results. No genuinely new listed stock clears the promotion bar. New policy evidence strengthens US-secure grid equipment and BWXT/microreactor exposure; crude weakened while refined-product scarcity remains the differentiated energy bottleneck.

macro.energy: WTI settled about $83.40 after a 4.2% weekly decline as Gulf crude exports recovered, but refined-product constraints remain much tighter than crude. Maintain integrated/refiner/product-logistics preference over generic upstream beta.
macro.gridPolicy: US Executive Order 14420 restricts risky foreign-produced bulk-power equipment and explicitly covers transformers, inverters, BESS, UPS, generators, turbines, breakers, relays and industrial controls. This is a structural tailwind for secure/domestic supply chains, though implementation rules are still pending.
macro.ratesValuation: Post-Jackson-Hole higher-yield discipline from the prior run remains relevant: favour backlog, current cash flow and customer-funded capacity over long-duration concepts.
macro.china: Selective AI/industrial investment continues; no evidence today supports a broad China-reflation upgrade.

categoryReads.Power / Grid: Strengthened by Executive Order 14420. Domestic/secure suppliers of bulk-power equipment gain strategic value; foreign/China equipment exposures face US-market policy risk. GEV/ETN/NVT/PWR and US-oriented secure supply chains remain preferred; do not automatically upgrade Chinese equipment names because US access may tighten.
categoryReads.AI / Data centres: Physical demand remains strong, but financing/ROI discipline remains central. The grid-security order adds supply-chain provenance as another constraint alongside time-to-power.
categoryReads.Nuclear: Army Janus Program awarded up to $2.2B across five vendors/sites for contractor-owned microreactors. This is a concrete commercialisation step rather than narrative-only support.
categoryReads.Uranium / Fuel: Structural fuel/enrichment thesis intact; no fresh contracting/price evidence today warrants a score change.
categoryReads.Oil & Gas: Crude weakened as Gulf exports recovered. Refined products remain the differentiated shortage, supporting XOM integration and tactical VLO/MPC/STNG/1138.HK more than pure upstream additions.
categoryReads.Metals: Copper/grid materials remain structurally supported, but no new metal equity clears the bar today.
categoryReads.Robotics / Automation: Commercialisation sequence unchanged: warehouse/fixed automation → cobots/mobile manipulation → industrial humanoids → open-world robots. Secure power/control supply chains add relevance to sensors, controls and power electronics but do not alter the sequence.
categoryReads.Malaysia: IOIPG is the material holding update. TNB/Southern Cable/YTL Power remain differentiated physical-stack exposures; DAYANG remains a wait-for-stabilisation holding.
categoryReads.Hong Kong / China: ASMPT remains preferred differentiated AI-infrastructure exposure. US grid-security restrictions are a new negative policy consideration for Chinese bulk-power equipment suppliers targeting the US.
